author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: A strong January payrolls print (467,000) pushed the 2Y Treasury up 16 bps in five observations to 1.31% and bear-flattened a still moderately steep curve (10Y-2Y +62 bps), while earnings split the market between companies with pricing power and data scale (Amazon +13.54%, Snap, Pinterest, Alphabet) and those with visibility gaps (Meta Platforms (FB) -21.42% over five sessions, PayPal -22.90%); with Russia-Ukraine risk carried mainly in oil and gas, China easing into a weak post-holiday economy and Poland caught between an inflation shield and rate hikes, the edition favours energy, banks and cash-generative platforms over long-duration growth, offshore China over onshore, and Polish banks over the rest of a stressed Polish market.
sources_policy: Evidence is limited to the frozen 2022-02-07 feed (tools/digest.py, all topics plus --grep searches) and the 2022-02-07 market card (tools/showcard.py). Every number is either a card value quoted exactly with its session tag (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-04 / 2022-01-28 for the Shanghai Composite; crypto prior completed daily close 2022-02-06; US Treasury prior close 2022-02-04) or appears in a headline cited in the same part. No other date's feed, card, spec, draft or note, no specs/, retail_drafts/, notes/retail_* or audit/independent_* files, and no web access were used. Previews (24/7 Wall St. BP/Pfizer/Sysco, ig.com Uber, Pekao MPC call, POLITICO on Macron's trip) are used only as pending events. Each citation ID is used at most twice (252 distinct IDs). No numeric spot-FX; currency direction only from dated reporting; DXY quoted as an index. Exclusions file for the date is empty. Process disclosure: during the survey a generic scratch file in the shared session scratchpad was overwritten by a concurrent process, so a partial printout briefly showed rows from other dates' cards (sessions 2022-01-31 and 2022-02-10); none of those values were used, and every quoted market value was re-read directly from showcard.py 2022-02-07 output stored in a uniquely named folder and checked against it. Verifier result: PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 WARN, 8,998 body words.
known_ambiguities_omitted: n0022 (RBA, '1 February 2022 | Minutes of the Monetary Policy Meeting'): minutes of the 1 February meeting are released weeks after the meeting, so the 1 February stamp is likely misdated/after-cutoff content; not used.

n1242 (Reuters, 'Bank of England raises rates by most since 1995 even as long recession looms'): wording matches a later, larger BoE decision rather than the 3 February 25 bp hike; treated as misdated; BoE covered via n1244 and n1239 instead.

n1278 (CNBC, 'Dollar up, euro down as pair face off in rate hike tussle', Sunday-stamped 6 February): contradicts the week's dollar weakness (DXY -1.84% over five sessions) and may describe Monday trading after the cutoff; not used.

n0803 (CNBC, 'Peloton stock surges on reports Amazon and Nike are among potential buyers'): the reported surge appears to postdate the completed regular-session close (PTON +1.44% on 2022-02-04), so the move cannot be quoted as a completed session; deal interest cited via WSJ n0770 instead.

n0826 (Motley Fool, 'Why Amazon.com Stock Popped 12% on Friday') and n0714 (Tubefilter, Spotify 'Stock Dropped 16% This Week'): figures conflict with completed card closes (AMZN +13.54% on the session; SPOT +0.84% over five sessions); card values used instead.

n1394 (UNSW Sydney, 'Russia's war in the Ukraine is complex and probably already underway'): an opinion that could be read as asserting an invasion as fact; on 7 February an invasion is only a pending risk; not used.
n0879 (TrendLife, 'A List of Fake Crypto Websites & Trading Platforms 2023'): title references a later year; misdated; not used.

Promotional or price-target items not used: n0947 (Fundstrat 'Bitcoin to $200k, Ethereum to $12k'), n0373 ('Bitcoin Price Predictions for 2025'), n0737 ('3 Hypergrowth Stocks That Can Soar 216% to 257%'), n0876 (Moomoo ''Snap' your fingers and gain 50% profit'), n0957 ('5 Cryptos to Watch'), n0943 (AVAX 'Headed for $75').

Numeric spot-FX items not used (direction only from n1587 and n1672, without magnitudes): n1630, n1631, n1632, n1545, n1583 (daily USD/EUR/CHF-PLN rate pages), n1725 (koruna/EUR-PLN hypothetical level), n1233 (EUR/USD), n1532.

Live-quote, live-blog or intraday pages not used as completed evidence: n1615 (Stooq WIG140), n1719 (Stooq GRAB.US), n0191 (MacroMicro LPR swaps), n0261 (FNN 'ASX down 0.3% at noon'), n1205 and n1226 (Reuters LIVE MARKETS), n0355 (eToro Shell quote page), n0249 and n0855 (eToro quote pages).

n1686 (Business Insider Polska, sell-off in an unnamed footwear company) and n1688 (Wyborcza.biz, unnamed 'biggest competitor of Biedronka and Lidl'): company not named in the title, so no company attribution was made.
n0044 (RBA SoMP '5. Economic Outlook', stamped 2 February although the Statement was published 4 February): not used; the SoMP is cited via n0064 (stamped 4 February 09:22 UTC).

Pending/after-cutoff events treated only as pending: China's Caixin January services PMI (due on the report day after the cutoff) is described as 'still to come' with no outcome; mainland China's first post-holiday session and all Monday Asian trading are not described; Macron's Moscow mission (n1280) and the Polish MPC February decision (n1706) appear only as pending catalysts; no date given for the next US CPI print because no dated preview exists.

Day-granular stamps accepted because the underlying event is clearly before the cutoff: n0145 (Caixin manufacturing PMI, stamped 29 January), n0135 (LPR cut, stamped 19 January), n0021 (RBA governor 'interest rates will go up', stamped 1 February), n2147 (tipswatch, Sunday-stamped, describing the prior session).
